page.title: Firewall
page.description: Filter web requests before they reach your apps. Rule changes apply right away, with no redeploy.

actionHint.allow: Skips every later rule, ban and bot check. Use it for trusted clients.
actionHint.challenge: Asks the browser to solve a short proof of work before it gets through.
actionHint.log: Counts the request and lets it continue. Use it to test a rule before enforcing it.
actionHint.rate_limit: Lets this many matching requests through per client, then answers 429 until the window ends.

lockout.title: This would block you
lockout.description: {{ip}} is the address you are using right now. Blocking it will lock you out of this control plane until the entry is removed from the server.
lockout.ruleDescription: This rule matches the address you are using right now. Saving it will lock you out of this control plane until the rule is removed from the server.

error.forbiddenTitle: You cannot see this part of the firewall
error.forbiddenHelp: Client addresses need the read:sensitive permission. Ask an administrator to add it to your role or token.

status.spikeSubtitle: Check the traffic tab, or turn on attack mode

chart.label: Requests by firewall outcome over the {{range}} range
chart.empty: No requests seen yet in this range. Counts appear as soon as traffic reaches a host.

alerts.title: Alerts
alerts.noneHelp: One appears here if blocked or challenged requests pass {{threshold}} per minute.
alerts.spikeHelp: {{rate}} blocked or challenged requests per minute over the last {{minutes}} minutes (alert at {{threshold}}).
alerts.attackOn: Attack mode is on. It ends

topList.spark: Requests over the last hour for {{key}}

traffic.note: Top tables are approximate and cover the last {{minutes}} minutes. They are kept in memory only, so they reset when the control plane restarts. Countries, networks and client fingerprints are not shown.
traffic.ipsEmpty: No requests seen in the last hour. Addresses appear here as traffic arrives.
traffic.deniedEmpty: Nothing denied, challenged or rate limited in the last hour.
traffic.userAgentsEmpty: No requests seen in the last hour.
traffic.pathsEmpty: No requests seen in the last hour.
traffic.hostsEmpty: No requests seen in the last hour.

bans.title: Temporary bans
bans.description: Clients that keep getting denied are blocked for a while.
bans.retention: A client denied {{strikes}} times within {{window}} is banned for {{duration}}. Bans live in memory and end on restart.
bans.emptyHelp: A client that keeps getting denied is banned here automatically, with a button to lift it.

rules.title: Rules
rules.customHelp: Checked in this order. The first rule that allows, denies or challenges ends the check. Changes apply without a redeploy.
rules.emptyHelp: Add a rule to deny, challenge, log or rate limit requests that match a path, header, user agent or address.
rules.deleteHelp: Traffic it matched is no longer filtered. This cannot be undone.
rules.hitsTitle: Matches since the control plane started
rules.hitsSpark: Matches over the last hour for {{name}}

ipList.blockHelp: Deny an address or range on every host, or only the host selected above.
ipList.bypassHelp: These addresses skip every other rule, ban and bot check.
ipList.required: Enter an IP address or CIDR range.
ipList.blockEmptyHelp: Add an address above, or block one from the Traffic tab.
ipList.bypassEmptyHelp: Add your office or monitoring addresses so a rule can never lock them out.
ipList.allHostsNote: New entries apply to every host.

bots.title: Bot management
bots.description: Turn the curated lists into log, challenge or block. Challenge shows a short browser check.
bots.badBotsHelp: Scrapers and scanners from the shipped list. Edit that list with the bot list setting on the server.
bots.aiBotsHelp: Crawlers that collect content for AI models. The list below is data you can edit.
bots.bansHelp: Ban a client for a while after it keeps getting denied.
bots.bansDetail: Ban a client for {{duration}} after {{strikes}} denials within {{window}}.
bots.listHelp: One user agent substring per line, matched without regard to case. Remove everything and save to go back to the shipped list.
bots.verifiedNote: Matching is by user agent only. Crawler identity is not verified, so a client can pretend to be a browser or a well-known bot.

attack.title: Danger zone
attack.description: Changes that affect every visitor of every host. They switch off by themselves.
attack.switchHelp: Tightens rate and connection limits and refuses the bad bot list on every host. Optionally challenges every visitor with a browser check.
attack.confirmHelp: It stays on for {{minutes}} minutes unless you turn it off sooner.
attack.consequenceLimits: Every client gets a low request rate and connection limit.
attack.consequenceBots: Bots on the bad bot list are refused.
attack.consequenceChallenge: Every visitor must pass a short browser check, including API clients.

limits.title: Limits for {{domain}}
limits.description: Per-domain rate, connection and body size limits, bot list and allowlist. These run after the firewall rules above.
limits.unknownDomain: This host is not configured here, so it has no per-domain limits.

audit.title: Firewall changes
audit.emptyHelp: Creating or changing a rule, an IP entry, bot handling or attack mode is recorded here with who did it.

editor.description: A rule matches when all its conditions do. Rules are checked in order, so add several rules for OR.

validation.nameRequired: Give the rule a name of up to 80 characters.
validation.rateCount: Enter a whole number of requests from 1 to 1,000,000.
validation.rateWindow: Enter a whole number of seconds from 1 to 3,600.
validation.paramName: Enter a name of letters, digits, dashes or underscores.
validation.valueRequired: Enter a value of up to 256 characters.
validation.ipInvalid: Enter an IP address or a CIDR range such as 203.0.113.0/24.
validation.methodInvalid: Enter an HTTP method such as GET or POST.
validation.countryInvalid: Enter a two letter country code such as DE.
